title: Chapter 109 — Promotions & Floor Execution
intro: Promo mechanics behind the scenes, event execution, and compliance.

sections.title: Promo Mechanics
sections.content:
Every promotion has terms: qualifying products, date range, minimum purchase, and how the customer receives the benefit — instant rebate, mail-in rebate, or gift card.

Know the terms cold. The customer who buys one day after the promo ends and discovers they missed a $300 rebate is a complaint waiting to happen. The rep who says 'this promotion ends Sunday — I want to make sure you get the rebate' is creating legitimate urgency.

Verify promo stacking. Can the manufacturer rebate stack with a store promotion? Can it stack with financing? Knowing the answer saves time at the register and prevents post-sale pricing adjustments.

sections.title: Floor Execution
sections.content:
When a promotion launches, the floor should reflect it within hours. Signage up. Feature displays merchandised. All reps briefed on qualifying products, terms, and talking points.

The huddle on promo launch day should cover: what is the promo, which products qualify, when does it end, and what is the one-sentence pitch for every customer. 'The Bosch rebate is live — every dishwasher customer should hear about it today.'

sections.title: MAP Compliance
sections.content:
Minimum Advertised Price policies restrict how low you can advertise a product. You can sell below MAP on the floor in a private conversation, but you cannot advertise below MAP in print, online, or social media.

Violating MAP can get your store dropped by the manufacturer. Know which brands enforce MAP aggressively — Bosch, Sub-Zero, Wolf, Miele, and others take it seriously. When in doubt, check with your manager before posting any price publicly.
